Original prompt: Build SORA CARS from FINAL_VERSION.mp4 as a complete Japanese arcade racer on SORA Nexus Taira, with wallet stakes, native Iroha result proofs and a SoraFS website.

# SORA CARS implementation

## Accepted scope

- 2–8 simultaneous human racers with visible opponents, contact/overtaking, drifting, braking and boost; 30 Hz deterministic physics, independent rendering and a 180-second limit.
- Three tracks, six equal-performance cosmetic variants, AI practice, public/private sessions, spectators, rematches, replays and history; keyboard, gamepad and mobile controls.
- Frequent supplied SORA flag/logo, Japanese identity and scenery, three original 1980s Japanese electronic-inspired compositions with local synthesis and downloadable MIDI files.
- Native Rust Iroha execution STARKs, no external zkVM; off-chain driving with on-chain escrow, accepted input/dispute history, proof, compact replay and atomic settlement.
- Wallet-local canonical Norito transactions through Iroha Connect, explicit network/profile pins and fee limits, replaceable signaling/proof workers, independently authenticated native finality verification.
- Qualified Taira rollout and native CID-only SoraFS publication with verified provider availability.

## Authoritative API correction

The user's latest architectural instruction supersedes the earlier race-specific ISI plan: **racing must not be an ISI**. Generic execution profiles, manifests, game sessions, participants, input certificates, disputes, escrow and settlement form the Iroha 3 platform. RaceV1 is the first application adapter. Native lifecycle code must not interpret cars, tracks, lap counts, boost or racing rankings. No race-specific native wire aliases remain.

Other games use the same lifecycle with another reviewed compiled relation and immutable manifest. Registration cannot install arbitrary verifier code or weaken parameters. Arbitrary deployed IVM programs are not yet provable. The active goal's original text predates this correction; this document records the accepted replacement scope.

## Authoritative first-release correction (September 6)

Iroha 3 and SoraFS are unreleased. The user explicitly forbids backward compatibility and authorizes changes directly on the sibling Iroha `optimizations` branch. Consolidate draft proof versions, codecs, admission and settlement into one corrected current design; remove compatibility-only aliases, decoder fallbacks and retirement/history support. Regenerate exact native profile identities, fixtures and proofs after source changes. Earlier dated V1/V2/V3 entries below are historical test evidence, not supported runtime versions or current qualification.

The canonical outcome ranks every eligible racer ahead of every forfeited racer, including a racer who finished before forfeiting. All-forfeit sessions have no winners and refund original stakes. Performance classes must constrain a reviewed common parameter set and exact equipment entitlement. Generic ISIs remain the reusable platform API.

SoraFS qualification requires native manifest registration, finalized provider ingestion, exact CID retrieval, integrity rejection and restart/availability tests. A local native CAR and verifier pass is only the packaging gate. No retired upload endpoint or unverified provider fallback may substitute for this flow. No live staked release or CID publication is claimed until actual rollout evidence exists.

## Added user scope: economy, story and language

- XOR-funded custom skins and upgrades, collectible NFT items and victory-based item transfers.
- Adopted defaults announced after optional questions: ranked races retain equal performance; performance builds use separately qualified classes. Only explicitly pre-staked NFTs transfer between opponents. These are implementation defaults and remain open to user steering.
- Japanese is the primary game language, with English dialogue subtitles. Six original Japanese adult characters have backstories and goals in an optimistic 1986 SORA Motor Club setting.
- Frequent exact supplied SORA flag and retro sun branding, including cars, track banners, menus, garage identity and cutscenes. The original gray-background retro sun is retained as a printed club badge; an inaccurate generated extraction was discarded.
- Three original locally bundled cutscene backgrounds, Japanese scripts/English subtitles, skippable dialogue and a free three-chapter podium campaign are implemented. Campaign progress is local and awards no XOR/NFTs.
- Native exact-price NFT sale offers, protected sale custody, atomic purchases and generic session item stakes are being implemented. There is no fabricated purchase or local-only NFT ownership claim.

## Rules and generation

A finisher wins ahead of unfinished racers. Without a finisher, a sole eligible survivor wins technically; at 180 seconds, the eligible greatest-progress cars share the prize. Exact ties differ by at most one indivisible asset quantum, assigned in increasing slot order. All-forfeit outcomes refund original stakes. Forfeited racers rank below all eligible racers even if they finished before forfeiting.

`npm run generate:native` uses a caller-selected native CLI to export the compiled graph and reference corpus. It rejects a binary whose embedded source identities differ from the sibling checkout. No hand-edited physics duplication remains in the browser. The compiled adapter registry binds each supported relation to its exact source identity. This goal turn made concrete progress from custody/history verification to ledger authentication. Read-only native review confirmed that the CommitQC post_state_root commits witnessed execution writes (or reads when there are no writes), not every WSV record. The ordinary witness namespace has no game-session record key; game::save emits only a projected event and directly inserts the full record. ## September 22 — image-derived region merging in the 3D POC

Continued the user's renderer correction with no new textures, scene composition,
geometry placement, light placement, default camera, controls or simulation changes.
The final POC now uses the new color/depth pixel-cluster pass with two rounds of
mutual adjacent-region merging. Each merge requires a real cardinal pixel boundary,
compatible color/depth and a combined area at most 64 pixels / extent at most 12×12.
The shader carries exact region areas and bounds in float MRT buffers, merges
area-weighted colors, and redirects pixel owners. Four MRT attachments and two

## September 22 — direction-aware pixel regions

The previous goal turn made progress: geometry-derived contours were implemented
and checked in the POC and actual racing. The full visual goal remains active.
The user explicitly requires renderer-generated pixel grouping rather than more
authored texture tricks; this continuation changes only the grouping/outline
pipeline, without changing composition, models, texture assets or controls.

Revisited [Kyprianidis et al.'s primary structure-tensor treatment](https://www.kyprianidis.com/p/tpcg2010/jkyprian-tpcg2010.pdf).
Its local minor eigenvector and eigenvalue contrast motivate the direction field
used here. This is a new original region-assignment implementation, not that
paper's full Kuwahara filter, not a new 2026 invention, and not its performance
result.

`PixelClusterPass` now computes a small structure tensor for each seed from the
lit frame, with Gaussian-weighted color-gradient products and depth-plane
rejection. Flat/low-energy neighborhoods have no directional bias. Confident
regions use an elliptical distance metric in assignments and prefer adjacent
merges along their local tangent. The merge area/bounds scale with seed spacing;
these constrain merges, not the maximum area of an initial assignment. A real
source member still anchors every representative's depth. Neither authored
brush maps nor random orientation fields enter this pass.

The initial seven-variant GPU study at
`output/browser/garage-poc/pixel-direction-study` conserves all 1,486,400 pixels
and exact area counts, with no invalid owners or GL/console errors. Direction5
has 36,909 active regions. Root inspected the default, larger-scale alternatives
and car crops. Changes are modest: floor/detail color regions become coarser,
but the car's broad panels still read as smooth rendered surfaces. This is not
a cutscene-fidelity pass.

A separate experiment amplified each region's color residual against neighboring
regions. Root rejected it because it made walls/floor blotchy without solving
the smooth car. Its source is retained only at
`tmp/fidelity/pixel-cluster-pass-rejected-region-contrast.ts`; it is removed from
the active renderer. Images remain in `pixel-direction-contrast-study`.

Tiny actual-GPU fixtures at `pixel-direction-synthetic` verify finite flat-field
output, correct tangent axes, zero region crossings at a depth split, exact
6,499-pixel mass/ownership on a 97×67 odd-sized image, repeatability and reversible
direction switches. The first harness result failed only because its empty HTML
requested a nonexistent favicon; the failed report is preserved. Adding an
inline empty favicon makes that same strict run pass without ignored errors.
After this run, derivative taps gained their own depth rejection and the disabled
merge path stopped reading direction data; those final refinements still require
the final run. Temporal coherence and racing performance remain unqualified.

## 2026-09-25 — pixel-art race renderer

The user approved the design in `docs/pixel-art-renderer.md` on September 25. Pixel Finish now selects a new pixel-art race renderer (`src/game/three/pixel-art/`) in Arcade and Tokyo; turning Pixel Finish off (or `?picture=clean`) still gives the clean frame. How it works:
- The detailed 3D scene renders at 2–3× a roughly 560×315 art grid (the short side is always 315). A depth-aware resolve gives each art cell one colour.
- The frame is tone-mapped once (Neutral at 1.3) and graded in OKLab. Band offsets are anchored in the world, and colours snap to a 128-colour palette from the cutscenes (`scripts/build-pixel-palette.mjs`, provenance in `palette.generated.json`).
- On top are selective outlines, lit rims, glints and small ramped glows in place of bloom, plus wet-road reflection columns with dashes and sparkles, and temporal hysteresis.
- The image is upscaled sharp-bilinear to the backing canvas, and the HUD is drawn after it at display resolution.
- Lighting moved to the cutscene mood: violet dusk sky, amber lamps, damp roads and a Tokyo sunrise.
- `?render=regions`, `?render=grouped` and `?render=cinematic` keep the earlier finishes for comparison.
- In pixel mode, 2D rain, splashes, petals, dust and speed lines snap to the art cells and use palette colours. Rain is drawn as vertical dashed columns of lavender cells, and the race paper grain is hidden.
- Native simulation, input, race arithmetic, HUD content, camera framing and object placement are unchanged.

- `npm test`: 390 of 404 pass. All 14 failures are the existing `ERR_IROHA_NATIVE_BINDING` source-provenance failures from the sibling native checkout.
- Playwright's bundled Chromium is missing, so `scripts/lib/browser-launch.mjs` retries with system Chrome (Metal). This also stops `tests/live-terms.test.ts` from hanging `npm test`; it now passes.

## 2026-09-26 — pixel-art race renderer: final build and review pack

This was the finalize stage for the pixel-art race renderer (Pixel finish, the default race picture in Arcade and Tokyo). No rendering code changed. The stage verified the build left by refine rounds 1 and 2, made the review pack, measured performance and finalised `docs/pixel-art-renderer.md`.

**Docs.** `docs/pixel-art-renderer.md` has a new "Final build" section:
- the pipeline and a stage table as built (`resolve → normals → carMask → surface → reflect → grade → carPaint → quantize → temporal → lines → carLines → glints → glow → cleanup → foliage → sparkle`);
- the per-frame inputs from `world.ts`;
- the decisions taken and the open ones;
- final performance and checks.

"Known limitations" was rewritten from the two critiques of refine round 2, which ran on this code.

What the build has gained since the 2026-09-25 entry (car, ground and sky stages, then two refine rounds; details in the docs):
- **Cars:** a mask; flat paint bands; red on the crimson ramp; navy glass; continuous lit rims and panel edges; lamp blocks with bezels and plates; distant cars as two livery tones with taillights.
- **Ground:**
  - World-anchored dashes at rest, and screen-row dashes at speed, so the road no longer boils.
  - Lamp pools drawn as sparse amber flecks over a violet floor instead of an orange wash. Hakone near road: L0.47 with 97% orange cells before, now L0.32-0.33 with 5-9%.
  - Analytic reflection columns under street lamps, and oil slicks.
- **Other stages:** analytic street-lamp heads with warm halos; a foliage stage; ink connect-or-drop; temporal hold with car-local and screen-space history; the wall motion filter.
- **Moods:** each Arcade track has its own mood, as the user approved: Hakone night, Yokohama harbour night (with a painted far shore and cranes), Nikko sunrise. Tokyo keeps its five chapters.
- **Small choices, by the user's "whatever looks cooler" rule:**
  - World rail rims are off. Beaded and "continuous" rims both dotted the stair-stepped rails, so the lighting draws lit rails as solid bars. Car rims stay continuous.
  - Lamp heads are flat cream ovals.
  - There are no OutRun-style forward bands.

Checks, 2026-09-26:
- `npx tsc --noEmit` passes.
- `npx tsx --test tests/pixel-art-*.test.ts`: 48 of 49 pass. The failure is the palette provenance test: the v3/v4 cutscenes are newer than `palette.generated.json`, and regenerating it is a lead decision.
- `npm test`: 416 of 431 pass. Fourteen failures are `ERR_IROHA_NATIVE_BINDING`, or native build-source provenance, from the sibling native checkout. The fifteenth is the palette provenance test.
- Browser tests:
  - `test-renderer-3d` passes.
  - `test-cinematic-runtime` passes.
  - `test-steering-direction` passes 73 checks.
  - `test-street-practice` passes 33 checks.
  - `test-speed-feel` passes when run alone (61 ticks in 2.02 s). Its first run, under a host load of 20-80 alongside captures and `npm test`, failed only the real-time 30 Hz tick-count check.
- `npm run build` passes, with the existing chunk-size warning.
- The six final pixel frames checked are palette-exact at cell centres (88-108 colours, 0 off-palette cells).
- Every capture, clip and perf run had 0 console, page and GL errors.

Performance: median `steps.wallMs`, clean and pixel alternated (the order swapped each round) on the M4 Max, 1-minute host load 7-12.

| Viewport | Arcade clean | Arcade pixel | Tokyo clean | Tokyo pixel |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1080p (5 rounds) | 36.1 ms | 31.8 ms | 32.7 ms | 28.3 ms |
| 960×600 (5 rounds) | 23.6 ms | 25.3 ms | 25.0 ms | 23.7 ms |
| 390×844 (3 rounds) | 20.7 ms | 19.5 ms | 23.4 ms | 22.7 ms |
| 844×390 (3 rounds) | 23.5 ms | 23.6 ms | 24.7 ms | 25.8 ms |

- At 1080p pixel art is 12-13% faster than clean.
- The phone-sized viewports are equal within noise; they ran on the desktop GPU, so they are not phone evidence.
- 960×600 Arcade is a watch item: pixel is 7% above clean, though the runs overlap (pixel 23.6-26.7 ms, clean 23.3-25.9 ms). At S = 2 the pass saves no scene pixels.
- Clean measured 41-48 ms at 1080p in earlier stages under heavier host load, so compare ratios rather than absolute times.

Evidence is in `output/browser/pixel-art/review/`. `index.md` lists every file with a caption.
- `frames/`: pixel and clean at 1080p for Arcade 0/1/2 and Tokyo night, at 2500 ms and 800 ms.
- `moods/`: the Arcade moods and all five Tokyo chapters.
- `sheets/`: side-by-side sheets with the cutscenes at equal art-cell density, and 4× car, lamp, ground, sky and facade crops.
- `motion/final/`: eleven 5-second, 60 fps clips of the production loop — pixel, quarter speed, clean, and pixel over clean.
- `perf/`.

Remaining gaps. The critiques scored style 6.5 of 10 and motion 6 of 10.
- **Open decision for the user: the wall motion filter.** It stops the wall strobe, but it smears facades and the SORA board's emblem at speed (`review/sheets/facades-at-speed-4x.png`). To try crisp walls: `window.__soraPixelArt.configure({ wallMotionFilter: 0 })`.
- **Style gaps:**
  - lamp-lit shoulders and pavements drawn as brick-like courses;
  - sunrise popcorn clouds as bright as the sun;
  - night darks blue-slate rather than plum, and frames darker than the cutscenes (Harbor p90 0.22-0.29 against 0.52);
  - false glow orbs on the teal rival's wheel;
  - black night canopies;
  - Harbor Run still reads as a tree-lined road;
  - zebra breaks in the reflection columns;
  - perforated overhead wires;
  - glints strung along sunlit rails;
  - saturated teal paint.
- **Motion gaps** (A-B-A against clean):
  - night canopies 2.5 ×;
  - rival cars 2.3-3 ×;
  - shop-tube halos re-roll at a stop;
  - the road while steering 2-3 ×;
  - walls between 40 and 60 km/h 2 ×.
  - Whole-frame A-B-A in the final clips is 1.9-4.6% against 0.9-3.3% for clean.
- **Needs the lead:** palette regeneration, and harbour scenery and lit windows.
